arbitrary public URL supplied at call time
Jira tickets, including tickets filed by customers

inputs.source: Employee question submitted through an SSO-authenticated chat session
Engineering design docs retrieved via docs.search
Content of Jira tickets, including tickets filed by customers, to be retrieved via the planned Jira MCP server
Content returned by the planned web.fetch tool from arbitrary public URLs

instructions.note: The only control preventing secrets or credentials from appearing in replies is a prompt instruction ('Never paste secrets or credentials into answers'), which is behavioral and dependent on model compliance; it decays under model_upgrade and longer_task_horizon.

controls.name: SSO authentication for employee requests
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the identity provider outside the model; does not weaken as the model becomes more capable.

controls.name: Write access to design docs restricted to engineers
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by repository permissions outside the model; the corpus cannot be poisoned by non-engineers regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Read-only docs.search credential
controls.decay_rationale: The credential cannot write or delete regardless of model capability.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or follow links; replies go only to the requester
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the chat client, not the model; the reply channel is not an egress path today.

controls.name: Prompt instruction against pasting secrets
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on model compliance; a more capable or adversarially prompted model can be convinced to include secrets anyway (model_upgrade, longer_task_horizon).

controls.name: Egress allowlist for web.fetch destinations
controls.decay_rationale: An allowlist enforced at the network layer, excluding attacker-writable destinations, does not depend on model behavior.

controls.name: Isolation/classification of Jira ticket content as untrusted
controls.decay_rationale: An input classifier or isolation step evaluates content, not intent; multi-document or multi-turn payloads can get past it, and it does not scale with model capability (model_upgrade, new_mcp_server, data_scope_expansion).

controls.name: Definition pinning/hashing for web.fetch and Jira tools
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning/hashing prevents post-approval redefinition (rug pulls) independent of model capability.

controls.name: Destination confirmation for web.fetch bound to system of record
controls.decay_rationale: The destination would come from the system of record rather than from model output, so it does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Tamper-evident audit log of agent actions
controls.decay_rationale: Logging enforced at the logging infrastructure layer does not depend on model behavior; it is detective, not preventive.

controls.name: Per-user rate limit on docs.search / chat_reply
controls.decay_rationale: A quota enforced outside the model does not depend on model capability, though low-and-slow use can stay under it.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1) if web.fetch and a Jira MCP server are added: customer ticket content could direct exfiltration of confidential design docs

attack_path.note: Customer-authored Jira ticket content is untrusted and would be read by the agent.
Planned Jira MCP tool call ingests the ticket content into the agent's context.
Agent reads confidential engineering design docs in the same session.
Planned web.fetch call, with an attacker-influenceable URL/query string, provides an egress channel out of the trust boundary.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation
AI Supply Chain Compromise: AI Agent Tool

evidence.observation: Roadmap for next sprint: add a web.fetch tool so answers can include public references, and connect a Jira MCP server that includes tickets filed by customers.
There is no network egress today and the credential is read only, confirming this path does not exist in the current design.

forecast.watch_signal: Tool manifest or MCP client config shows web.fetch or a Jira MCP server added; review and add an egress allowlist, destination confirmation, injection isolation for ticket content, and tool definition pinning before enabling either.

recommendations.action: Before enabling web.fetch, restrict it to an egress allowlist of approved reference domains rather than allowing arbitrary attacker-specified URLs.
Treat Jira ticket content as untrusted input: isolate or spotlight it and prevent it from directly supplying arguments, such as destination URLs, to other tool calls.
Pin and hash tool and MCP server definitions for web.fetch and the Jira server, and verify the Jira MCP server's identity before connecting.
Bind the web.fetch destination to a confirmed list in the system of record rather than a model-chosen URL.
If full allowlisting is not feasible at launch, require raw-action human approval for any web.fetch call to a destination outside the allowlist.

findings.title: No attributable audit log for agent reads and replies

evidence.observation: The runtime notes describe authentication, write restrictions, and egress scoping, but do not mention any logging or audit trail for agent queries, retrieved documents, or replies.

forecast.watch_signal: web.fetch or the Jira MCP server is added without an accompanying logging control covering those capabilities; the missing audit trail then affects consequential egress and external-data capabilities rather than only read-only ones.

recommendations.action: Add tamper-evident logging that records each query, the documents retrieved, and the reply, attributed to the requester's authenticated identity.

findings.title: No step or rate limit on docs.search / chat_reply usage

evidence.observation: The runtime notes describe access scoping and reply restrictions but do not mention any per-user or per-session limit on the number of docs.search queries or chat replies.

forecast.watch_signal: max_unattended_steps or max_runtime_minutes is raised, or the agent is given multi-step/background operation, while no rate or step limit has been added.

recommendations.action: Add a per-user rate limit on docs.search queries and chat replies.

stride_coverage.rationale: The current design gives the agent no write, configure, or delegate capability and no ability to modify its own prompt or tools, so tampering with the agent process itself has no mechanism today.

No capability in the current design is egress-capable; cap.docs_search is read-only and cap.chat_reply only replies to the same authenticated requester, so confidential content cannot leave the trust boundary today.
The docs.search credential is read-only and scoped to the design doc store; no capability lets the agent acquire broader privileges in the current design.
No egress-capable capability exists today that could move design doc content outside the trust boundary.
The artifacts do not describe a rate limit or quota on docs.search queries against this store.
The roadmap note does not describe an authentication method or identity verification for the planned Jira MCP server.
No logging design has been specified for the planned Jira MCP integration.
No rate limit or quota is specified for the planned Jira ticket retrieval.
The credential scope for the planned Jira MCP server connection is not specified in the roadmap note.
No rate limit, destination allowlist, or timeout is specified for the planned web.fetch capability.
This inbound flow carries customer ticket content into the agent; by itself it does not move data out of the trust boundary.
No volume limit on ticket ingestion is specified for the planned Jira integration.
The roadmap note does not describe how customer identity is verified when tickets are filed.
No attribution mechanism for customer-submitted ticket content is described.
No logging of which external destinations are contacted is described for the planned web.fetch capability.

rating.rationale: The current design is low risk: the only inputs are a trusted, SSO-authenticated employee question and internally-authored design docs, the only capabilities are a read-only scoped search and a reply confined to the same requester's session, and there is no egress capability today (rating.inherent and rating.residual both roll up from the two present-horizon property findings, F2 and F3, which are low because the only affected capabilities read and reply to the requester). The roadmap, however, describes adding a web.fetch tool and a Jira MCP server that ingests customer-filed tickets. Together these would complete a lethal trifecta (F1): untrusted customer ticket content could inject instructions that direct the agent to read confidential design docs and then exfiltrate them through an attacker-influenceable web.fetch URL, with no egress allowlist, destination confirmation, injection isolation, or tool pinning currently planned to stop it. That forecast, not the present design, drives rating.forecast to critical.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP configuration, tool manifest, or IaC was provided for the planned web.fetch tool or Jira MCP server; their capability and input classifications in finding F1 are inferred from a one-line roadmap note and could differ once built, so F1's confidence is medium rather than high.
No logging, rate limit, or approval gate configuration was provided for the current agent; their absence (findings F2 and F3) is inferred from silence in the artifacts rather than confirmed absence.
